chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Yaʿqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) for Friday. He said: It is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) in travel and residence, unless the traveler fears the cold for himself.

key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: the state of being resident and not traveling
key_terms.الْقُرَّ: intense cold that may cause harm
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an obligation
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the ritual bath associated with Friday

ai.seo_question: Is Friday ghusl recommended for a traveler, and is there an exception due to cold?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Friday ghusl is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), recommended both while traveling and while residing. An exception is made for the traveler if he fears harm from the cold, indicating consideration of hardship in ritual practice.
